Rashi on Berakhot 15b:10:1.hebrew: לעולם ר' יהודה אפי' לכתחלה מכשיר - ודמגילה — רבי יוסי היא, ואפי' דיעבד נמי פסיל; והא דתורם לכתחלה — ר' יהודה; והא דברכת המזון — דרביה הוא, דאמר ר' יהודה משום רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: ״צריך להשמיע לאזנו״, והאי לישנא לכתחלה משמע, אבל דיעבד — יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:10:1.english: Actually, Rabbi Yehuda deems [it] valid even ab initio - And that [mishnah] of Megillah is [according to] Rabbi Yosei, and he invalidates [it] even after the fact; and that [baraita where a deaf person] separates terumah ab initio is [according to] Rabbi Yehuda; and that [baraita] of the Grace after Meals is [the view of] his teacher, for Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: "[One] must make [it] audible to his ear," and this phrasing implies ab initio, but after the fact he has fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:11:1.hebrew: השתא דאתית להכי - דאשמעתן הא פלוגתא דר"מ:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:11:1.english: Now that you have arrived at this - That you have informed us of this dispute of Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:11:2.hebrew: אפי' תימא ר' יהודה - דאמר בק"ש ״יצא״ — דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא; ומתני' דמגילה — לכתחלה היא דפסלה לחרש, ור' יהודה היא; והא דברכת המזון נמי — ר' יהודה היא; ודקא קשיא לך: הא דר"י בריה דר' שמעון בן פזי, מני? — ר"מ היא, דמכשיר לכתחלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:11:2.english: Even if you say Rabbi Yehuda - For he said regarding the recitation of Shema, "[he has] fulfilled [his obligation]" — after the fact, yes; ab initio, no; and the mishna of Megillah — [it is only] ab initio that it disqualified a deaf person, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda; and that [baraita] of the Grace after Meals is also [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda; and as for what was difficult for you: That [baraita] of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi — in accordance with whose [opinion is it]? — [it is] Rabbi Meir, who deems [it] valid ab initio.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:12:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יהודה - דק"ש, שלא השמיע לאזנו, יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:12:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - That regarding the recitation of the Shema, [one] who did not make it audible to his ear has fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:13:1.hebrew: הוה אמינא - דרבי יהודה לכתחלה נמי אמר, והאי דאפליג דיעבד — משום דרבי יוסי:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:13:1.english: I would have said - That Rabbi Yehuda said [one may do so] even ab initio, and this [fact] that he disputed [in the case of] after the fact [was] because of Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:14:1.english: And he has no remedy - Even after the fact.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:15:1.english: In other mitzvot - In all the blessings.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:18:1.hebrew: ההוא - הסכת ושמע בדברי תורה כתיב, כדאמרי' בפ' הרואה (ברכות ד' סג:): כתתו עצמכם על דברי תורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:18:1.english: That [verse] - "Pay attention and hear" is written with regard to words of Torah, as we say in chapter HaRoeh (Berakhot 63b): "Break yourselves over words of Torah."

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:19:1.english: And was not precise - That he stammers.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:1:1.hebrew: ולכתחלה הוא דלא הא דיעבד שפיר דמי - ובהא איכא למימר דאפילו ר' יהודה מודה, דלא שמעינן דפליג בק"ש אלא דיעבד:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:1:1.english: And ab initio [it] is that [he may] not, but after the fact [it] is acceptable - And regarding this, it can be said that even Rabbi Yehuda concedes, for we have not heard him disagree regarding the recitation of Shema except after the fact.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:20:1.hebrew: הלכה כדברי שניהם להקל - הלכה כר' יהודה, דלא בעי שמיעה; והלכה כר' יוסי, דלא בעי דקדוק:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:20:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with the statements of both of them to rule leniently - The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who does not require hearing; and the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who does not require precision.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:21:1.hebrew: שאול ועוצר רחם - פסוק הוא בספר משלי: ״שלש הנה לא תשבענה״:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:21:1.english: The grave and the barren womb - This is a verse in the Book of Proverbs: "There are three that are never satisfied."

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:21:2.english: A womb takes in - The semen, and brings forth the child.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:22:1.hebrew: שמכניסין בו בקולי קולות - של בכי ומספד:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:22:1.english: Into which they bring [the deceased] with loud cries - Of weeping and lamentation.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:23:1.english: And you shall write them - That the writing should be flawless and complete.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:23:2.hebrew: ואפילו צואות - שבפרשה, כגון וקשרתם וכתבתם, צריך לכתוב בתפילין ומזוזות:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:23:2.english: And even commands - That are in the passage, such as "And you shall bind them" and "And you shall write them," one must write [them] in tefillin and mezuzot.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:24:1.hebrew: דאמר לך מני - הא דאצטריך ליה קרא לרבות צואות לכתיבה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:24:1.english: The one who said [this] to you, who is he? - This [matter], that he required a verse to include commands for writing.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:24:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה היא - דשמעינן גבי כתיבת פרשת סוטה, משום דלא כתיב ביה וכתבתם אלא וכתב, דאמר: אלות — אין, צואות — לא, כגון והשביע אותה הכהן ואמר הכהן, דתנן (סוטה ד' יז), רבי יהודה אומר: כל עצמו אינו כותב אלא יתן ה' אותך לאלה ולשבועה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:24:2.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda - For we have heard regarding the writing of the portion of the sota — because it is not written in it "And you shall write them," but rather "And he shall write" — that he said: Curses, yes; commands, no — such as "And the priest shall adjure her, and the priest shall say" — as we learned in a Mishna (Sotah 17a): Rabbi Yehuda says: He writes nothing at all except: "May the Lord make you a curse and an oath."

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:25:1.hebrew: משום אלה הוא - דמשמע מיעוטא. הא לא כתיב מיעוטא, הוה משמע כולה מלתא מוכתב. והכא דליכא מיעוטא, למה ליה לרבויינהו מוכתבתם:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:25:1.english: It is because of "these" - For it implies an exclusion. Had an exclusion not been written, the entire matter would have been implied from "and he shall write" [vekhatav]. And here, where there is no exclusion, why was it necessary to include them [the commands] from "and you shall write them" [ukhtavtam]?

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:27:1.hebrew: בין הדבקים - תיבות המדובקות זו בזו, אם אינך מפרידן. כשהתיבה השניה מתחלת באות שהתיבה שמלפניה נגמרת, הוא קורא אותן שתי אותיות באות אחת, אם אינו מתעסק ליתן ריוח ביניהן, כדמפרש רבא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:27:1.english: Between adjacent [words] - [These are] words that adhere to one another if you do not separate them. When the second word begins with the [same] letter with which the preceding word ends, he reads those two letters as one letter if he does not take care to leave a space between them, as Rava explains.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:29:1.hebrew: בפרש שדי - אם תפרש שדי ותבדיל תיבות של מלכות שמים. מלכים בה תשלג בצלמון — התורה אשר בה מלכים ימלוכו, תשלג ותצנן לך את צל המות:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:29:1.english: When the Almighty scatters - If you clearly enunciate [the name] Shaddai and separate the words of [the acceptance of] the Kingdom of Heaven. “Kings over it, it will snow in Tzalmon” — the Torah, through which kings reign, will snow and cool down for you the shadow of death [Gehenna].

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:4:1.hebrew: מדסיפא ר' יהודה - דקתני ר' יהודה מכשיר בקטן:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:4:1.english: Since the latter clause is Rabbi Yehuda - For it is taught: "Rabbi Yehuda deems a minor fit."

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:5:1.hebrew: ודילמא כולה ר' יהודה היא וחסורי מחסרא והכי קתני הכל כשרין לקרות את המגילה חוץ מחש"ו - והא כדאיתא, והא כדאיתא:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:5:1.english: And perhaps the entire [mishna] is Rabbi Yehuda, and it is missing [text], and it teaches as follows: All are fit to read the Megilla except a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor - And this [case] is as it is, and that [case] is as it is [each according to its own rule].

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:5:2.hebrew: בד"א - דקטן לכתחלה לא — בקטן שלא הגיע לחנוך, אבל הגיע לחנוך — אפי' לכתחלה שרי. הגיע לחנוך מצות — כגון בן תשע ובן עשר, כדאמרינן ביומא פרק בתרא (ד' פב.):
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:5:2.english: In what [case] is this said? - That a minor [is] not [permitted] ab initio — [this is said] with regard to a minor who has not reached [the age of] training; but [if he] reached [the age of] training, even ab initio it is permitted. [One who has] reached [the age of] training for mitzvot [is], for example, [a child] nine years old or ten years old, as we say in Yoma, the last chapter (82a).

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:6:1.english: In accordance with what did you establish [it] - [This refers] to the mishna of Megillah.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:6:2.hebrew: כרבי יהודה - ואשמעת לן, דכי אמר ר' יהודה בק"ש יצא, דיעבד קאמר, ולא לכתחלה:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:6:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - And it teaches us that when Rabbi Yehuda said regarding the recitation of the Shema, "he has fulfilled [his obligation]," he was saying [that it is valid only] after the fact, and not *ab initio*.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:6:3.hebrew: אלא הא דתני כו' תורם - ואע"פ שהוא צריך לברך ואין אזניו שומעות — מני:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:6:3.english: However, that which was taught, etc., [he may] separate terumah - And even though he needs to recite a blessing and his ears do not hear [it] — in accordance with whose [opinion is it]?

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:8:1.hebrew: אלא מאי - בעית למימר דר' יהודה היא, דק"ש אפי' לכתחלה קאמר, כי היכי דתיקו הא דר' יהודה בריה דר' שמעון בן פזי אליביה; והאי דאפליגו בדיעבד — להודיעך כחו דר' יוסי:
Rashi on Berakhot 15b:8:1.english: Rather, what - You wish to say that it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda, who said that [regarding] the recitation of Shema [it is permitted] even ab initio, so that that [baraita] of Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi will stand according to his view; and this [fact] that they disputed [in the case of] after the fact [was] to make known to you the strength of Rabbi Yose.

Rashi on Berakhot 15b:8:2.english: However, that which was taught, etc. - In accordance with whose [opinion is it]?

Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:15:1.hebrew: אבל בשאר מצות יצא - וא"ת: הא לעיל אמר דשאר מצות ילפינן מק"ש, כגון תרומה ומגילה וברכת המזון? וי"ל: דרב יוסף פליג אסוגיא דלעיל:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:15:1.english: "But with regard to other mitzvot, he has fulfilled [his obligation]" - And if you say: Surely above [the Gemara] said that we derive other mitzvot from the recitation of Shema, such as terumah, Megillah, and the Grace after Meals? And one can answer: Rav Yosef disagrees with the sugya above.

Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:27:1.hebrew: בין הדבקים - רב אלפס מוסיף: כגון "וחרה אף", דאם לא יתן ריוח אז נראה כמו "וחרף". וכן מוסיף: "וראיתם אותו", "וזכרתם את", "ועשיתם את" — שצריך ליתן ריוח בין מ"ם שבסוף תיבה לאל"ף שבתחלת תיבה שאחרי'. וכן צריך להתיז זיי"ן של "תזכרו", שלא ישמע שי"ן — למען שיהיה לנו שכר מצות, ואין לנו לעשו' על מנת לקבל פרס:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:27:1.english: Between adjacent [words] - Rav Alfas adds: For example, "vecharah af" ["and His anger will burn" (Deuteronomy 11:17)], for if one does not leave a space, then it appears like "vecheref" ["and he blasphemed"]. And so too he adds: "ure'item oto" ["and you shall see it"], "uzkhartem et" ["and you shall remember"], and "va'asitem et" ["and you shall do"] (Numbers 15:39–40), where one must leave a space between the mem at the end of a word and the alef at the beginning of the word that follows it. And so too, one must sharply pronounce the zayin of "tizkeru" ["so that you remember" (ibid. 15:40)], so that it does not sound like a shin [tiskeru, "that you receive wages"] — [as if the verse meant:] "so that we should have the reward of the mitzvot," and we ought not to perform [mitzvot] on condition of receiving a reward.

Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:5:1.hebrew: דילמא ר' יהודה וחסורי מחסרא וכו' - תימה, דאין זה בשום מקום דקאמר חסורי מחסרא ולאוקמי אליבא דחד תנא; ועוד, לוקמיה כר' יוסי ובלא חסורי מחסרא. וי"ל: משום דלקמן פסקינן כר' יהודה, לכך ניחא לאוקמיה אליבא דר' יהודה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 15b:5:1.english: "Perhaps it is Rabbi Yehuda, and it is missing [text], etc." - [This is] astonishing, for nowhere does [the Gemara] say "it is missing [text]" [merely] to establish [a mishna] according to a single Tanna! And furthermore, let [the Gemara] establish it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, and without [positing that] it is missing [text]! And one can answer: Since below [on 15b] we rule in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, therefore it is preferable to establish it according to Rabbi Yehuda.
